sections.text:
1 Titulus ad extremam tantum capituli partem convenit (cf. p. 192, 18 ss.). Quod
iam animadvertit lector quidam qui in margine codicis Angelici scripsit : Κεφάλαια
διάφορα χρήσιμα εἰς διαφόρους χρήσεις. Revera excerpta esse ex opere Iuliani
Laodicensis crediderim, cuius nomen et in titulis capitum Περὶ πολέμου (supra
p. 183, 15) omissum est. Nam p. 190, 6 legitur Πάλιν δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς Ἰουλιανὸς λέγει,
etsi prius in textu astrologus ille non commemoretur. Haec coniectura ideo
quoque quadrare videtur quod p. 190, 6 verba quaedam Procli anno 484 mortui
proferuntur. Scimus enim Iulianum extremis saeculi V annis scripsisse. Vide supra
p. 171, infra p. 195; cf. etiam ad 189, 23.
sections.en:
1 The title suits only the very end of the chapter (cf. p. 192, 18 ff.). Which
a certain reader already noticed who wrote in the margin of the Angelicus codex: Various
chapters useful for various uses. Indeed I would believe that they are excerpted from the work of Julian
of Laodicea, whose name was also omitted in the titles of the chapters On war (above
p. 183, 15). For on p. 190, 6 is read And again the same Julian says,
although earlier in the text that astrologer is not mentioned. This conjecture therefore
also seems to square because on p. 190, 6 certain words of Proclus who died in the year 484
are brought forward. For we know that Julian wrote in the last years of the 5th century. See above
p. 171, below p. 195; cf. also on 189, 23.

summary.headline: Zodiacal Sign Classifications
summary.text: Astrological rules for choosing zodiacal signs according to the nature of persons, affairs, places, times, and occupations, including tropical, solid, bicorporeal, diurnal, nocturnal, masculine, feminine, rational, irrational, Hermetic, wet, fiery, equinoctial, and trine classifications. The apparatus discusses excerpts attributed to Julian of Laodicea, references Proclus, and records readings from the Angelicus codex.
